Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

refugee noun

also refugees, fugitive, displaced person, asylum seeker

classical

Sall. C. 6.1: Trojānī, quī Aenēā duce profugī sēdibus incertīs vagābantur
Liv. 34.60: patriā profugus (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. refugee

profugus, profugī m.

the adjective profugus, profuga, profugum, used as a noun, declension

one who has fled home or country, a refugee

In prose an adjective, “fled”, with the place in the ablative (profugus domō, Liv. 1.1); as a noun chiefly in verse and comedy (Plaut. Trin. 3.2.75, Ov.). Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens and Egger give it for the modern refugee.

Other words

  • exsul, exsulis m. and f. — an exile, a banished person

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.75: Ephesum ad Antiochum vēnisset exsul (Lewis & Short); Cic. Clu. 175: vagus et exsul

    One sent away from home by law or by force; a refugee who chose to flee is rather profugus.

  • perfuga, perfugae m. — a deserter to the enemy

    noun, first declension · avoid · classical

    Not a refugee: one who goes over to the other side (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Trojānī, quī Aenēā duce profugī sēdibus incertīs vagābantur

    the Trojans, who under Aeneas’ leadership were wandering as refugees, with no settled homeSall. C. 6.1
